clips.text: Why is the sky blue? It is a very good question, and the answer starts with the sun.
Sunlight looks white. But it is really every colour at once, all mixed together.
When that light reaches our air, it bumps into it, and gets bounced about in all directions.
Here is the trick. Blue light bounces about far more than red or yellow light does.
So wherever you look, blue light is coming at you, from every part of the sky. And that is why it looks blue.
And at sunset? The light has to go the long way through the air. The blue gets lost on the way, and the reds and oranges are what is left.
